To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the newborn, the dynamic intracellular calcium pool is not accessible to the contractile mechanism of smooth muscle cells.
the density of IP3 receptor binding sites is reduced in the newborn period compared with the adult.

in the feline anstrum, the newborn has less IP3 receptor density than the adult, and that the newborn is able to release calcium from the intracellular stores in a fashion similar to that of the adult.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the gastrointestinal tract and the role of the enteric nervous system.
the role of calcium and its intracellular stores in smooth muscle function.
the mechanisms of gastrointestinal motility in the neonate and the changes that occur in the mechanisms of motility during the transition from the fetal to the postnatal period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the feline newborn circular smooth muscle is able to contract, in the presence of thapsigargin and in the absence of external calcium, because the intracellular stores are intact and accessible.
in the adult, IP3 receptors are more numerous than in the neonate.
, in the adult, the smooth muscle of circular antral muscle is capable of responding to myogenic agonist stimulation in the absence of external calcium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the feline antryal smooth muscle is a useful model for studying the development of the gastrointestinal tract and that the differences in the response to calcium agonists and antagonists between newborn and adult animals is due to differences in the ability of the smooth muscle cells to release calcium from intracellular stores and not to the lack of a functional calcium store.
, in the adult, IP3 receptors are located on the sarcoplasmic reticulum and that the IP3 receptors in the newborn are located in the plasma membrane, where the receptor density is markedly decreased.

the development of the feline gastrointestinal smooth muscle is characterized by a progressive maturation of contractile responses to a variety of stimuli, including myogenic and neurogenic agonists, and that the mechanisms of contraction are similar in adults and newborns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the newborn antrum is able to respond to myo-kinetic agonists in a manner similar to the adult antrum if extracellular calcium is present.
the smooth muscle in the newborn feline antral circular layer is capable of generating an increase in [Ca2+]i in response to myogenic stimuli.

the smooth muscle of feline newborn antra has a lower density of IP3 receptors than the adult, which may be related to the inability of the newborn smooth muscle cells to release calcium from intracellular stores.
